adversarial_verification.method: Every cited test file/function in the discoverer's S10 coverage report was opened and read against the production path it names. Each 'none' was re-checked with an independent repo-wide grep for the key identifier/behaviour. The S10-5 probe was additionally executed (go test -tags audit7 -run TestZ15RateLimiterCheckAllocatesNothing) to establish whether it is currently red or green.
adversarial_verification.corrected_semantics: 'corrected' is true when the discoverer's verdict changed OR a material claim in the entry was factually wrong (e.g. a non-existent test name).
verdict_changes: S10-5: direct -> partial. The cited test asserts allocs == 0 (absence of the described defect) and PASSES today (measured allocs/call=0.0); a fix implementing the recommendation leaves it green, so it does not pin the described defect.
non_verdict_corrections: S10-3: cited test name TestCompressedLargeBody does not exist; corrected to TestCompressesLargeBody.
uncited_findings_found: S10-1 only: an untracked round-9 verification artifact (internal/httpapi/zz_audit9_inflight_planes_test.go, TestAudit9OneAddressHoldsTheWholeInFlightCapAcrossPlanes) does exercise two planes from one peer and pins the defect. It is not a committed regression test (untracked, pins the buggy behaviour rather than the recommended fix), so the partial verdict stands with this note.

findings.corrected_note: Verdict confirmed. Both cited tests were opened: TestInFlightCapIsSharedPerClient (internal/httpapi/inflight_share_test.go:16-70) drives Server.withInFlightLimit with maxInFlight=2 and sends every request to /v1/me (same plane), and TestZ11OneAddressCannotHoldEveryInFlightSlot (internal/zzprobe/audit7/z11resiliencedos/inflight_test.go:32-118) keeps A's first and second requests on /oauth/token. Because both keep each peer on one plane, both tests pass unchanged when the counter is re-keyed on aggregateClientKey alone (the recommended fix): A's second same-plane request is still refused and B is still admitted. They exercise the production path but do not assert the cross-plane sum the finding describes, so partial stands. Independent grep for MaxInFlight/bucketKey/withInFlightLimit found one additional in-tree file, internal/httpapi/zz_audit9_inflight_planes_test.go (untracked, created during round 9), whose TestAudit9OneAddressHoldsTheWholeInFlightCapAcrossPlanes does saturate two planes from one peer (2x /oauth/token + 2x /v1/me at maxInFlight=4) and asserts the whole-cap grab (held==4) plus the other peer's 503. That is a verification oracle pinning the defect, not the committed regression guard for the recommended fix, and it is untracked; it is recorded here but not counted as coverage. The committed default suite still misses the cross-plane harness the gap_note asks for.
findings.asserts: Drives Server.withInFlightLimit with maxInFlight=2 (perClient=1) and asserts that one client's SECOND request is refused 503 while a DIFFERENT client is still admitted. Both requests are sent to the SAME path /v1/me, i.e. the same (plane, client) key. A second, socket-level guard exists at internal/zzprobe/audit7/z11resiliencedos/inflight_test.go (TestZ11OneAddressCannotHoldEveryInFlightSlot, build tag audit7): source A holds its one slot via a slow /oauth/token body, its second /oauth/token is refused, and 127.0.0.2 is served. It too keeps every request from A on the protocol plane.
findings.gap_note: Both tests only exercise one plane per client, so they pass unchanged with the cited defect present. None sends the SAME source address to TWO namespaces (e.g. one slow slot under /oauth/token plus one under /v1/...) and then checks that a third client is still admitted. Harness needed: at Server level with maxInFlight=2, park one request from peer A on /oauth/token and one from the same peer (same RemoteAddr / client key) on /v1/me, then assert a request from peer B is admitted and that A's summed in-flight count across planes cannot exceed perClient; a version against the real Handler() chain would also prove the shared semaphore is globally exhausted by A.

findings.corrected_note: none confirmed by independent greps. (1) `panic(` in every *_test.go under internal/zzprobe and internal/httpapi: no readiness probe panics (the only deliberate panic is panickyFederation.AllSources, used to drive /v1/sources, not Ready). (2) Every `Ready:`/ReadinessProbe literal in the whole test tree (internal/httpapi/health_test.go, internal/zzprobe/verifyhttpedge/zzprobe_p14_test.go, audit6/z06httpedge/readiness_test.go, audit7/z11resiliencedos/readyz_poison_test.go, audit7/z11verify/readyz_race_test.go and probe_session_store_test.go, audit7/z12verify/verify_readyz_test.go, audit7/z12configstartupobservability/readyz_test.go, audit7/z18gohazardsweep/probes_test.go, audit7/z18verify/verify_test.go, internal/zzprobe/startup/startup_probe_test.go): every probe returns normally, honours ctx.Done, or is released before the test ends. (3) No test function name references Panic/Wedge/Stuck/Hang in a readiness context. No test issues a follow-up /readyz after a panicking or deadline-ignoring probe, so readinessCache.check's abnormal exit (running=true, settled never closed) is unreached.
findings.asserts: No test installs a ReadinessProbe that panics. health_test.go (TestReadyzTracksTheProbe, TestReadyzAnswersUnderLoadRatherThanShedding, TestReadyzDoesNotLeakTheProbeError) only uses probes returning nil/error; internal/zzprobe/audit6/z06httpedge/readiness_test.go, internal/zzprobe/startup/startup_probe_test.go, internal/zzprobe/audit7/z11resiliencedos/readyz_poison_test.go and internal/zzprobe/audit7/z18gohazardsweep/probes_test.go use probes that block or fail but always RETURN, so readinessCache.running is always cleared and settled always closed.
findings.gap_note: No test reaches readinessCache.check's abnormal exit, so the c.running=true / c.settled-never-closed wedge is unverified. Harness needed: healthServer/newFullConfig with Ready set to a func(context.Context) error that panics (the httpapi recoverer must be installed so the first request becomes a 500 rather than killing the test), then issue a second GET /readyz after readinessTTL and assert it returns a fresh 503 "not ready" (or 200) rather than 503 "checking" forever; a variant with a probe that blocks past readinessTimeout while ignoring probeCtx would pin the blocking half.

findings.corrected_note: Verdict confirmed (none), but the cited test name was wrong: there is no TestCompressedLargeBody; the test is TestCompressesLargeBody (internal/compress/compress_test.go:136). A repo-wide `panic(` grep of every *_test.go finds no handler panicking through compress.Compressor.Handler (the only panics in internal/compress are a helper panic on NewWrapper failure in spike_gzhttp_test.go:155, gated behind the unreachable gzhttpspike spike), and no test instruments coding New/Close/Put or counts releases. The named tests exist and cover only the normal path: TestPoolReuseRoundTrips:314, TestFlushStartsCompressing:333, TestCompressesLargeBody:136, BenchmarkSingleLargeWrite:408.
findings.asserts: internal/compress/compress_test.go never panics a downstream handler. TestPoolReuseRoundTrips and BenchmarkSingleLargeWrite only cover the normal return path where cw.finish() runs and releases the pooled gzip/zstd writer back through c.release. TestFlushStartsCompressing, TestCompressesLargeBody (formerly cited as the non-existent TestCompressedLargeBody) etc. likewise return normally. No test instruments encode/release counts and none drives next.ServeHTTP to panic after the 1 KiB threshold committed an encoder.
findings.gap_note: The panic-after-commit path (finish/release skipped, zstd encoder Close never called, writer never returned to sync.Pool) has no test. Harness needed: compress.Compressor.Handler wrapping a handler that writes >DefaultMinSize bytes with Content-Type application/json and then panics, with the compressor (or a fake Encoding) counting New/Close/Put so the assertion can see whether the writer was released and the pool refilled; run under a recover so the panic is absorbed, then assert the next compressed request reuses a Reset writer and that Close was called once per acquired writer.

findings.corrected_note: Verdict confirmed. Opened internal/httpapi/breach_test.go:30-147: it signs in, reads csrf_token from GET /v1/sessions/current, walks specRoutes() with Accept-Encoding: gzip and a canary, gzip-decodes each body, then asserts only (a) no body contains a secret AND the canary and (b) no compressed response echoes the canary; lines 24-29 and 133-138 state explicitly that the check is independent of whether a secret-bearing response was compressed. Adding Cache-Control: no-transform to /v1/sessions/current or /v1/device/verification leaves it green. Independent grep of every Content-Encoding assertion in the tree (internal/httpapi/compression_test.go, plane_test.go:208, zz_audit_httpapi_test.go, zz_audit9_compress_bypass_test.go, internal/compress/*, internal/zzprobe/audit6/z06httpedge/compress_test.go) shows none targets /v1/sessions/current or /v1/device/verification; the compression tests cover the /app/ shell, the protocol-plane exclusion and generic small/large bodies.
findings.asserts: Signs in, reads the CSRF token from GET /v1/sessions/current, then walks every spec route (/v1/sessions/current and /v1/device/verification included) with Accept-Encoding: gzip, a canary in query/header/body, and asserts (a) no response body contains both a secret (CSRF token, session cookie, bearer) and the canary, and (b) no response that declared Content-Encoding echoes the canary. It gzip-decodes the body first. It deliberately does NOT assert whether the CSRF-bearing responses were compressed (comment: the check is independent of compression).
findings.gap_note: No test pins the compression state of the secret-bearing business responses, so adding Cache-Control: no-transform to /v1/sessions/current or /v1/device/verification (the recommended fix) would leave every existing test green. Needed: a test that asserts the actual nosniff/no-transform behaviour for these endpoints, e.g. GET /v1/sessions/current with Accept-Encoding gzip and a session cookie must NOT return Content-Encoding gzip/zstd (and Vary must not advertise Accept-Encoding), plus a positive control showing an ordinary large business response still compresses; alternatively assert that the CSRF-bearing handler sets no-transform so the compressor's skip signal is exercised.

findings.corrected_note: Verdict downgraded direct -> partial. The cited assertion is `if allocs > 0 { t.Errorf("CONFIRMED: Check allocates ...") }`, i.e. it asserts allocs == 0, the ABSENCE of the described defect. It was executed: `go test -tags audit7 -count=1 -run TestZ15RateLimiterCheckAllocatesNothing -v ./internal/zzprobe/audit7/z15performancecapacity/` logs 'Check(tracked key): allocs/call=0.0, 0 B/op' and PASSES. Implementing the recommendation (drop the ReserveN reservation / allocation) leaves it green, so under the stated rubric it does not pin the described defect and cannot be direct. It is strongly related (same path, same quantity) and would fail only if the allocation (re)appeared, which is a regression guard, not a red confirmation oracle. This is also consistent with verify/S10.json, which measured 0 allocs/op and rejected the finding. The weaker companion BenchmarkCheckExistingKey (internal/ratelimit/ratelimit_test.go:183) only calls b.ReportAllocs() and asserts nothing.
findings.asserts: Builds ratelimit.New(1000, 100), admits the key once (anti-vacuity: Verdict.Allowed and Size()==1), then measures testing.AllocsPerRun(2000, func(){_ = l.Check(key)}) on the tracked-key path and errors with 'CONFIRMED: Check allocates ... per request' when allocs > 0. It exercises exactly the cited Limiter.Check path and measures the cited quantity, but it asserts allocs == 0 (the defect absent), passes today (verified: allocs/call=0.0), and would stay green under the recommended fix; it therefore does not pin the described defect. A weaker non-asserting companion is BenchmarkCheckExistingKey in internal/ratelimit/ratelimit_test.go, which only calls b.ReportAllocs(). (File is under //go:build audit7, so it does not run under a default `go test ./...`.)
findings.gap_note: No test is RED while the described allocation is present, so there is no direct confirmation oracle for the finding's claim; the only related test is an invariant-direction zero-allocation guard that asserts the opposite. A test that truly pins the described defect would assert allocs > 0 (or that the reservation escapes) on the tracked-key path and fail today. Note verify/S10.json rejects the finding empirically (0 allocs/op for both Check and a raw ReserveN sequence), so such a red test cannot be written against this build.
